source_text: Commode nobiscum ageretur, si aut apud eruditos iudices negotium veritatis tueri daretur facultas aut, quia hoc interim negatur, vel nullo imperitorum obverberaremur tumultu.
pass_a_gloss: It would be treated fairly with us, if either the faculty of guarding the cause of truth before learned judges were given, or, because this is denied in the meantime, we were at least battered by no tumult of the unskilled.
pass_b_english: We would be treated fairly if we were allowed to defend the cause of truth before educated judges—or, since that is denied us for now, if at least we were not battered by the uproar of the ignorant.

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at 2.1; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
